title: NSE IPO Expected to Price at ₹1,700–1,785 Per Share in One of India's Biggest-Ever Listings
excerpt: The National Stock Exchange's long-awaited initial public offering could value the world's most active derivatives exchange at up to $46.4 billion, with listing expected the week of September 21.
body:
• NSE is expected to price its IPO at ₹1,700 to ₹1,785 per share, valuing the exchange at up to ₹4.4 trillion ($46.4 billion)
  • The listing is targeted for the week starting September 21, with book-building expected to begin September 11 and the price band announcement on September 15
  • The offering will be a pure offer-for-sale with existing shareholders selling about 5.5% of equity — no fresh capital will be raised
  • NSE shares currently trade at approximately ₹2,050 in the unlisted market, with a grey market premium of ₹255

India's National Stock Exchange is expected to price its landmark initial public offering at ₹1,700 to ₹1,785 per share, according to sources cited by Reuters and Bloomberg, setting the stage for one of the country's largest-ever stock market listings.

At the upper end of the price band, NSE would be valued at approximately ₹4.4 trillion ($46.4 billion), potentially placing it among India's ten most valuable listed companies. The IPO is expected to rank alongside billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms as one of the biggest public offerings in Indian capital markets history.

Timeline Takes Shape

The exchange received long-awaited regulatory approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India on September 4, clearing a path that had been blocked for years by regulatory concerns. Reuters reported last week that NSE is targeting a listing in the week starting September 21.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2Y2M-6oX6uk

Book-building is expected to begin on September 11, with the formal price band likely to be announced on September 15. The anchor book may open on September 17, with public subscription potentially starting September 18 and listing on September 25, according to reports citing anonymous sources.

What Investors Are Getting

The IPO will be structured as a pure offer-for-sale, with existing shareholders selling approximately 5.5 percent of the exchange's total equity capital — down from an originally planned 6 percent, Bloomberg reported. No fresh equity will be raised, meaning all proceeds go to selling shareholders.

Key sellers include some of India's largest financial institutions: State Bank of India, General Insurance Corporation of India, Bank of Baroda and National Insurance. These institutional shareholders stand to reap a combined windfall of approximately $2.6 billion from the listing.

NSE has more than 200,000 existing investors, and its shares currently trade at approximately ₹2,050 in the unlisted market. The grey market premium stood at ₹255 on Tuesday, down from ₹285 over the previous two days amid a weakening secondary market and the start of a lock-in period for pre-IPO investors.

"Post-listing, NSE will be top 10 among India's largest companies in terms of market cap, which will garner huge interest from the market."

— Deven Choksey, Managing Director, DRChoksey FinServ

A Dominant Market Position

NSE operates India's benchmark Nifty 50 index and dominates the country's equity derivatives market. It is the world's most active derivatives exchange by number of contracts traded, processing billions of transactions annually.

The exchange's listed rival BSE has seen its shares surge 28-fold since going public in 2017, providing a reference point for the kind of re-rating investors may anticipate.

At an expected price-to-earnings valuation of around 35 times, analysts see meaningful headroom for gains after listing. In informal meetings, large prospective investors including Indian mutual funds indicated comfort buying shares at around ₹1,800 apiece, suggesting strong institutional demand at the expected price band.

What to Watch

The pricing represents a discount to private market valuations, where NSE has been valued at roughly $55–57 billion based on unlisted market trading. That built-in discount, combined with the exchange's dominant market position and growth trajectory, is expected to drive strong subscription numbers.

However, the timing adds an element of uncertainty. The broader market has fallen sharply this week on crude oil and geopolitical concerns, which could affect IPO sentiment in the near term. The final pricing decision will be taken after investor roadshows and closer to the listing date.
